data.content:
The Blazor Web App is ready. Here's what was created:

**Architecture:** Interactive WebAssembly with server prerendering — pages render server-side on first visit (fast load), then WebAssembly takes over for client-side interactivity (no server round-trips).

**Project structure:**
```
ShipmentTracker/
├── ShipmentTracker/          (Server host)
│   ├── Endpoints/            (REST API for shipments)
│   ├── Data/                 (EF Core + SQLite, seed data)
│   └── Components/           (Layout, Home, Account pages)
└── ShipmentTracker.Client/   (WebAssembly client)
    ├── Pages/
    │   ├── Dispatcher.razor       (Dashboard with filter/status update)
    │   ├── CreateShipment.razor   (New shipment form)
    │   └── TrackShipment.razor    (Customer tracking + progress bar)
    ├── Models/ShipmentDto.cs
    └── Services/ShipmentService.cs
```

**Key features:**
- **Roles:** `Dispatcher` (full CRUD) and `Customer` (view own shipments + track)
- **Auth:** ASP.NET Identity with individual accounts
- **Demo accounts:** `dispatcher@shiptrack.com` / `Dispatch1!` and `customer@example.com` / `Customer1!`

Run with: `cd ShipmentTracker/ShipmentTracker && dotnet run`
